question: 5 HR 20 MIN 20 SEC corresponds to a longitude difference of:
The time is 1830 UTC on 2 December, the Standard Time and date in Hong Kong 2219N 11412E is:
explanation: Hong Kong standard time = UTC + 8: 1830 + 8 h = 0230 on 3 December.

question: Daylight Saving Time (Summer Time):

options.text: Is used to extend the sunlight period in the evening.
Is introduced by setting the standard time forward by one hour.

explanation: Summer time is used in some countries, advances standard time (usually 1 h) and extends evening daylight — all three are correct.

question: At 2200 Standard Time, 15th August in Brasilia 1600S 4800W, the Standard Time and Date in Kwajalein Island (Marshall Islands) 0900N 16740E is:
explanation: Brasília UTC −3 → 2200 + 3 = 0100 UTC 16 Aug. Kwajalein UTC +12 → 1300 on 16 August.

question: If the Mean Sun moves 121° 30 along the Equator, that equals:
Twilight:

options.text: are periods when it is nearly dark.
are periods when it is too dark to move around without artificial lighting.
are the periods when an observer is illuminated by both direct and indirect rays of light from the sun.
are the periods before sunrise and after sunset when the light is lower than when the sun is above the horizon.

explanation: Twilight is the period before sunrise and after sunset when the sky is still lit by scattered light although the Sun is below the horizon.

question: The suns moves from East to West at a speed of 15° longitude an hour. What ground speed will give you the opportunity to observe the sun due south at all times at 6000N?
explanation: The Sun moves 15° of longitude per hour. At 60°N 15° = 900′ × cos 60° = 450 NM per hour → 450 kt westbound.

question: On the 27th of February, at 52° S and 040° E, the sunrise is at 0243 UTC. On the same day, at 52° S and 035° W, the sunrise is at:
explanation: Same latitude, so sunrise occurs at the same LMT. 75° further west = 5 h later in UTC: 0243 + 5 h = 0743 UTC.

question: The times given for Sunrise, Sunset, Morning and Evening twilight in the Air Almanac:

options.text: Must always be corrected for atmospheric refraction.

explanation: Almanac sunrise/sunset/twilight times are tabulated in LMT (for a given latitude), then converted to UTC using longitude.

question: Some standard times may differ from UTC by other times than whole hours, because:

options.text: some areas have limited communication with neighbouring areas, which does not call for co- ordinated standard times.
the political authorities have emphasised the importance of the sunlight period in a particular position.
it has been considered highly desirable that the sunlight period of the day is balanced around noon, standard time.

explanation: Half-hour (or other) offsets exist for local reasons — limited coordination, political choice, balancing daylight around noon — all three are correct.

question: A day is by definition:

options.text: the period from morning to evening.
the period from sunrise to sunset.
the period in which day flying is authorised.
the period elapsed between two successive transits of a heavenly body.

explanation: A day is the interval between two successive transits of a heavenly body (sun, mean sun or star) across the same meridian.

question: Mean time has been introduced in order to:

options.text: Compensate for the irregularities of the speed of rotation of the Earth around it is axis.
Have one fixed time to be used within the border of a country.
Introduce a constant measurement of time, independent of the daily variations in the movement of the Sun as observed from the Earth.
Save us the problem of adjusting our watches entering every leap year.

explanation: The real Sun's apparent speed varies through the year; mean time uses an imaginary mean sun moving at constant speed.

question: What is the meaning of the term standard time?

options.text: It is the time zone system applicable only in the USA.
It is an expression for local mean time.
It is another term for UTC.
It is the time set by the legal authorities for a country or part of a country.

explanation: Standard time is the time legally set for a country or part of it.

question: A is at longitude 01230E and B is at longitude 04315E. LMT in B is 1749. What is the LMT in A?
explanation: D.long = 30°45′ = 2 h 03 min. A is west of B so its time is earlier: 1749 − 0203 = 1546.

question: The International Date Line is located:

options.text: At the apparent suns anti meridian.
At the 180° E/W meridian, or in the vicinity of this meridian.
At all latitudes on the 180° E/W meridian.

explanation: The date line follows the 180° meridian, deviating around land groups so that a country keeps one date.

question: G is in position 3500N 03445W. For a particular date sunrise at 3500N is in the Air Almanac listed as 0715. What is the time of sunrise at G, given in UTC?
explanation: Almanac times are LMT. 34°45′W = 2 h 19 min. UTC = 0715 + 0219 = 0934 UTC.

question: An aircraft leaves Guam (13° N 144° E) at 23:00 ST on 30th April to fly to Los Angeles, California, USA. If the flight time is 11 hrs 15 mins what is the Standard Time and date of arrival in Los Angeles?
explanation: Guam UTC+10: 2300 ST = 1300 UTC 30 Apr. +11 h 15 → 0015 UTC 1 May. Los Angeles in April keeps daylight time (UTC−7) → 1715 on 30 April.

question: Apparent Time is:

options.text: The correct time, as it appears on our watches and clocks.
Based on the time of transit of the apparent Sun.
The time that is apparent to everybody; in other words the official time.
The average time, calculated from the movements of the Sun and the stars.

explanation: Apparent (solar) time is based on transits of the real ("apparent") Sun.

question: A day at a place as measured in local mean time starts:

options.text: when the mean sun transits the meridian of the place in question.
when the mean sun transits the Greenwich meridian.
when the mean sun transits the anti meridian of the place in question.
when the mean sun transits the 180E/W meridian.

explanation: An LMT day starts at local midnight, i.e. when the mean sun transits the anti-meridian of the place.

question: The LMT and date at a longitude of 00100W is 1330 on the 6 January, what is the LMT and date at a longitude of 15900E:
explanation: D.long 001°W → 159°E = 160° = 10 h 40 min, east so later: 1330 + 1040 = 0010 on 7 January.

question: What is the time (UTC) of sunrise on 6th December at Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada (50° N 123° W)?
explanation: Sunrise at 50°N on 6 Dec ≈ 0742 LMT. Longitude 123°W = 8 h 12 min → 0742 + 0812 = 1554 UTC on the 6th.

question: Civil Twilight occurs between:

options.text: sunset and 6 deg below the horizon.
6 deg and 12 deg below the horizon.
12 deg and 18 deg below the horizon.

explanation: Civil twilight: Sun's centre from the horizon to 6° below (sunset to end of civil twilight).

question: What is the UTC time of sunrise in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada (49N 123 30 W) on the 6th December?
explanation: Sunrise at 49°N on 6 Dec ≈ 0738 LMT. 123°30′W = 8 h 14 min → 0738 + 0814 = 1552 UTC.

question: By the term "lower transit" (of a heavenly body) it is understood that:

options.text: the body is passing the meridian of the observer or another specified meridian.
the body is passing the anti meridian of the observer.
the body is at the same celestial meridian as another body.

explanation: Lower transit = the body crossing the observer's anti-meridian (for the Sun, local midnight).

question: What is the Standard Time in Hawaii when it is 0600 ST on the 16th February in Queensland, Australia?
explanation: Queensland UTC+10: 0600 16th = 2000 UTC 15th. Hawaii UTC−10: 1000 on the 15th.

question: What is the definition of Morning Civil Twilight?

options.text: The period in the morning, just before sunrise.
Morning civil twilight is the period in the morning from the centre of the sun is 6° below the horizon until the upper limb of the sun appears at the horizon.
The period when the sun, in the morning, has its centre between 6° under the horizon and the horizon.
The period of semi-darkness in morning.

explanation: Morning civil twilight runs from Sun's centre 6° below the horizon until sunrise (upper limb on the horizon).

question: In which two months of the year is the difference between the transit of the Apparent Sun and Mean Sun across the Greenwich Meridian the greatest?
explanation: The equation of time peaks in mid-February (≈ −14 min) and early November (≈ +16 min).

question: An aircraft departs Hong Kong 2219N 11412E at 2234 Standard Time on the 17 April. If the flight time is 11 hours 17 minutes, the Standard Time and date of arrival at Honolulu (Hawaii) 2125N 15755W will be:
explanation: Hong Kong UTC+8: 2234 = 1434 UTC 17 Apr. +11 h 17 → 0151 UTC 18 Apr. Honolulu UTC−10 → 1551 on 17 April.

question: What is the Local Mean Time at 65° 30N 123° 45W at 22:00 UTC on 6th September?
explanation: 123°45′W = 8 h 15 min (W → subtract): 2200 − 0815 = 1345 LMT on the 6th.

question: It is noon Standard Time in Norfolk Island 2900S 16755E on 16 July. What is the LMT and date in Johnston Island 1644S 16932W:
explanation: Norfolk Island (UTC+11½ in the Air Almanac used): noon = 0030 UTC 16 Jul. Johnston 169°32′W = −11 h 18 → 1312 LMT on 15 July.

question: The duration of twilight:

options.text: Will in the period around the Equinoxes increase as you approach the equator from North or South.
Is generally longer in positions at high latitudes that in positions at lower latitudes.
Is independent of the suns declination, and only depends on the observers latitude and longitude.
Is longer in the morning than in the evening, because of the refraction in the atmosphere.

explanation: The Sun crosses the horizon more obliquely at high latitude, so twilight lasts longer there.

question: What does 5 hours 50 minutes and 20 seconds change of longitude represent?
The Equation of time?

options.text: States the difference in time of transit of the Mean sun and the Apparent sun any particular day.
States the difference between celestial time and apparent time.
Is used to calculate mean time when standard time is known.
Is used when calculating the difference between UTC and LMT.

explanation: The equation of time is the difference between mean time and apparent time (mean sun vs apparent sun transit) on a given day.

question: What is the local mean time, position 65° 25N 123° 45W at 2200 UTC?
How long time does it take for the Mean Sun to move from meridian 14515E to meridian 02345W?
The length of a apparent solar day is not constant because:

options.text: The Earths speed of revolution in its orbit varies continuously, due to the orbit being elliptical.
The Earths speed of rotation is not the same at all latitudes.
The Suns declination is not constant.
The plane of the Ecliptic and the plane of the Equator are inclined to each other.

explanation: The Earth's orbital speed varies (elliptical orbit), so the apparent solar day varies in length (the tilt of the axis also contributes).

question: Consider the following statements on Sunrise and Sunset.

options.text: At equator sunrise and sunset occur at quite regular times throughout the year.
In May sunrise occurs later at 4500N than at 4500S.
In November sunset occurs earlier at 4500S than at 4500N.
In July the period of sunlight is longer at 1500S than at 1500N.

explanation: At the Equator day and night are always ≈ 12 h, so sunrise/sunset times are fairly regular all year.

question: The Local Mean Time at longitude 095° 20W, at 0000 UTC, is:
explanation: 095°20′W = 6 h 21 min 20 s → 0000 UTC − 6:21:20 = 1738:40 on the previous day.

question: The countries having a standard time slow on UTC:

options.text: will often have an earlier standard date than the UTC date.
will generally be located at western longitudes.
will often experience sunrise earlier than the sunrise occurs at the Greenwich meridian.
will generally be located at eastern longitudes.

explanation: Time "slow" on UTC (behind UTC) is found at western longitudes.

question: UTC stands for:
explanation: UTC = Co-ordinated Universal Time.

question: At 1200 Standard Time on the 10th July in Queensland, Australia, what is the Standard Time in Hawaii, USA?
explanation: Queensland UTC+10: 1200 = 0200 UTC 10 Jul. Hawaii UTC−10 → 1600 on 9 July.

question: A flight departs Auckland (New Zealand) 3650S 17446E, at 0600 Standard Time on the 23 January. The flight time is 9 hours 27 minutes, the Standard Time and date of arrival at Santiago (Chile) 3300S 07100W will be:
explanation: NZ standard time UTC+12: 0600 23 Jan = 1800 UTC 22 Jan. +9 h 27 → 0327 UTC 23 Jan. Santiago UTC−4 → 2327 on 22 January.

question: The mean sun:

options.text: Is the middle position of the sun.
Has a declination equal to the apparent sun.
Moves with constant speed along the celestial equator.
Is only of interest to users of astronomical navigation.

explanation: The mean sun is an imaginary sun moving at constant speed along the celestial equator.

question: When approaching the International Date Line from the East, you:

options.text: should be prepared to increase your date by 1.
should increase your date by an extra date at the first midnight you experience.
should be prepared to decrease your date by 1.
should not change date at the first midnight you experience.

explanation: Crossing the date line westbound (approaching from the east) you add one day.

question: Consider the following statements on sunset:

options.text: For positions at the same longitude, sunset will occur simultaneously at all latitudes.
At sunset the centre of the sun is at the observers horizon.
Sunset is the time when the observer at sea level see the last part of the sun disappear below the horizon.
Night-flying regulations start at the time of sunset.

explanation: Sunset is when the upper limb of the Sun disappears below the horizon for a sea-level observer.

question: 5 hours 20 minutes and 20 seconds hours time difference is equivalent to which change of longitude:
Sun rise at 50° N 072° E is at 0254 on 25th January. What time will the sun rise at 50° N 007° E on that day?
explanation: Same latitude → same LMT of sunrise. 65° further west = 4 h 20 min later: 0254 + 0420 = 0714 UTC.

question: On 4 February the Air Almanac lists 1941 as the time of sunset at 5000S. An observer register sunset at 2113 UTC this day. What is the observers position?
explanation: Sunset LMT 1941; observed 2113 UTC → 1 h 32 min = 23° west of Greenwich.

question: 0000 hours mean time of an observer is when:

options.text: the mean sun is in transit with the observer’s meridian
the apparent sun is in transit with the observer’s meridian
the mean sun is in transit with the observer’s anti-meridian

explanation: Local mean midnight (0000 LMT) is the lower transit of the mean sun — its passage across the observer’s anti-meridian. Noon (1200 LMT) is the upper transit.

question: When the time is 2000 UTC, it is:
explanation: 090° = 6 h. West of Greenwich subtract: 2000 − 0600 = 1400 LMT. (090°E would be 0200 next day; 030°W would be 1800.)

question: What is the ICAO definition of night?

options.text: From half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise
The period between the end of evening civil twilight and the beginning of morning civil twilight, or such other period as may be prescribed by the appropriate authority
Any period decided upon by a national aviation authority

explanation: ICAO Annex 2: night is the hours between the end of evening civil twilight and the beginning of morning civil twilight, or another period prescribed by the authority.

question: What determines the local mean time of sunrise and sunset at any location on Earth?

options.text: The time of year, and the longitude and elevation of the location
The time of year, the latitude and the elevation of the location

explanation: In LMT, sunrise/sunset depend on the date (declination), latitude and observer elevation — not longitude (longitude only matters when converting to UTC).

question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: At any given spot the Sun will sink below the horizon earlier at sea level than at altitude
Sunrise and sunset occur at the same LMT along a given meridian for the same elevation
At any given spot the Sun will sink below the horizon later at sea level than at altitude
The LMT of sunrise and sunset along a parallel is independent of elevation

explanation: An observer at altitude sees further over the horizon, so the Sun sets later for him — i.e. earlier at sea level.
